Subject: Eval synthesis — throughput vs precision tradeoff (post-demo notes)

Thanks again for carving out time this morning, Ari — quick recap and proposed next steps.

TL;DR:
- Best-fit candidate models: LlamaX-13B-FT (baseline), LlamaX-6.9B-FT (cost-optimized), and Mistral-Eval-7B (high-efficiency).
- Quantization options we recommend trialing in priority order: AWQ 4-bit (best perf/cost balance), GPTQ 4-bit (safer accuracy), FP8 (experimental perf for long-context workloads).
- Attached: your raw benchmark dump + our prompt set and a one-page tradeoff matrix.

What we observed in the demo:
- Latency: With batching disabled, LlamaX-13B median token latency ~60ms on your 80-token average prompt. LlamaX-6.9B ~35ms.
- Accuracy: On your 1k eval prompts LlamaX-13B baseline hit your correctness threshold on 82% of items; LlamaX-6.9B was at ~76% (some systematic drop on multi-step arithmetic).
- Quantized runs: AWQ 4-bit on LlamaX-13B reduced tokens/sec cost by ~2.6x with an average quality delta of -1.8% (measured by your rubric). GPTQ 4-bit was slightly higher quality (-0.9% delta) but ~1.9x cost improvement. FP8 runs showed minimal latency gains on wider sequences but produced non-deterministic token probabilities on a small subset (we flagged 12/1000 prompts).

Recommended next steps (week):
1) Run a focused pilot (2–3 days) comparing LlamaX-13B (AWQ4) vs LlamaX-6.9B (GPTQ4) on your top-200 prompt set. We’ll provide the infra and a reproducible benchmark harness.
2) Let Redwood run an FP8 exploratory pass on 50 long-context prompts where you care about throughput — we’ll isolate cases where FP8 diverges.
3) Joint evaluation sync Wednesday (10/20) to decide production variant and guardrails (confidence thresholds, fallback to baseline).

Action items: can you confirm which team member will drop the production prompt set into the Drive link below? If you prefer, we can also accept a secure upload to your S3.

Links and attachments: 
- Shared bench dashboard: https://redwood-internal.app/benchmarks/finlytics/2027-10-v2
- Attachment: finlytics-bench-v2.csv (raw results), finlytics-promptset-v1.json (repro prompts), redwood-quant-tradeoff-matrix.pdf (one-pager)

Thanks — jonas

Perfect — thanks for the quick turn. Two technical clarifications and an operational note from our side: 

Technical notes:
- AWQ vs GPTQ: In our internal infra AWQ tends to preserve logits ordering well for classification-style outputs while offering better memory packing. GPTQ sometimes retains slightly higher top-k token probabilities which matches the smaller measured quality delta you saw. Practically, AWQ = better TCO; GPTQ = safer accuracy for edge prompts.
- FP8 caveat: the FP8 backend requires careful kernel selection; in our experience it performs best when sequence lengths > 512 and with stable attention patterns. We'll sandbox it on your long-context subset only.

Operational note:
- Rollback / guardrail plan we propose: per-request scoring hook that compares response confidence and a small checksum against baseline responses; if confidence delta > 0.35 or schema mismatch occurs, route to LlamaX-13B (baseline) and log the event in the Console. We'll include a flag to enable auto-fallback for the pilot.

I'll kick off the pilot configuration once Leo shares the final prompt set. For the pilot, we'll run three arms: 
A) LlamaX-13B baseline (FP32), 
B) LlamaX-13B (AWQ4), 
C) LlamaX-6.9B (GPTQ4).

Expected deliverables at the end of the pilot (48–72 hrs): 
- Per-prompt confusion matrix and delta heatmap, 
- Token-level cost and latency breakdown across arms, 
- Flagged failure cases with deterministic reproduction steps.

Jonas

One small engineering note on the quantization matrix we attached: 

- When comparing AWQ and GPTQ 4-bit on LlamaX-family weights, we noticed two pattern classes where AWQ underperforms relative to GPTQ: (1) tightly-coupled arithmetic chains and (2) long open-ended generation where token entropy is high. Those correlate with the regression set Ari flagged.
- Mitigation we recommend for the pilot: enable selective per-prompt dequantization. Mechanism: tag prompt IDs in your prompt set that are sensitive (we can auto-detect candidates) and run those through a higher-precision fallback path (FP16) while others use AWQ/GPTQ variants.

Operational considerations: pilot infra will be provisioned under your Dedicated sandbox; estimated incremental cost for the three-arm pilot is ~$2.1k for the test window (we'll issue a trial credit if you prefer to keep it neutral).

Happy to hop on a short call tomorrow morning to walk through the per-prompt tagging approach.

— Aditya
